rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are the allied groups that attacked, arriving in anger and malice to rout the Muslims.
rows.anchor: refer to the groups among the allies who had attacked

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God routed the attackers; their ambitious plans did not materialize at all.
rows.anchor: they had great plans but none of them materialized even slightly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took the Muslims' place in fighting the dangerous assault, defeating the enemy through violent winds and a powerful angelic force.
rows.anchor: He inflicted a crushing defeat on the enemy through tempestuous winds and a powerful army of angels

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls the sūrah's opening assurance that God is sufficient as guardian; believers should trust Him, and He will aid them through nature and angels when they pursue His cause.
rows.anchor: found in the opening verses of the sūrah. God is powerful and dominant;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurayẓah had made a peace treaty with the Muslims, then broke it and joined the attacking confederates after Ḥuyy ibn Akhṭab persuaded their leader Kaʿb ibn Asad.
rows.anchor: the Banū Qurayẓah broke their treaty and became allies of the attackers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuyy told Kaʿb that this was their best chance to eliminate the Muslims and that losing it would bring regret.
rows.anchor: Ḥuyy further told him that this was their best chance to eliminate the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurayẓah's nearby forts and many fighters greatly strengthened enemy morale and made the Muslims' ordeal more severe, but God routed them too.
rows.anchor: Their participation boosted the morale of the enemy many times, and this became a very enduring trial for the Muslims.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After returning from the battle, the Prophet ordered an immediate attack; after a siege of about twenty-five days, the Qurayẓah accepted Saʿd ibn Muʿādh as arbitrator, whose verdict executed battle-capable men and enslaved women and children.
rows.anchor: Muslims laid siege around them and this lasted almost twenty five days. Finally, being awe-struck

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṣiyāṣ means a rooster's claw; its plural can mean an ox's horns and came to denote citadels, forts, and garrisons.
rows.anchor: refers to the claw of a cock. Its plural

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God planted such fear in their hearts that they did not resist Saʿd's verdict; the Muslims killed their fighting men without resistance and enslaved the rest.
rows.anchor: God implanted the awe and fear of the Muslims in their hearts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims received the Qurayẓah's entire territory, including their homes, forts, and other property.
rows.anchor: The Almighty consigned their whole territory including their houses, forts and all other assets to the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of land not yet reached foretells later conquests, including Khaybar, Makkah, Rome, Syria, and other places.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the conquests of Khaybar, Makkah, Rome, Syria and other places.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the Muslims witnessed assured them that God can accomplish His intentions and no one can stop Him; believers should therefore trust Him fully.
rows.anchor: what the Muslims saw with their eyes was enough to give them this satisfaction that God has power over all things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next section turns from the previous call for Muslims to obey God and the Prophet to the Prophet's wives, warning them against hypocrites who would instill materialism.
rows.anchor: In the previous section, Muslims were asked to unite in showing obedience to God and His Prophet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wives were chosen to transmit the divine laws and wisdom learned from the Messenger; fulfilling their duties brings great reward, while wrongdoing brings especially severe punishment.
rows.anchor: God has chosen them for the companionship of His Messenger so that they can become a means of delivering the divine laws and wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zayd-Zaynab episode continues the previous section's concerns: hypocrites stirred up questions and mischief, and God's answers clarify important aspects of religion.
rows.anchor: this also relates to what has been discussed in the previous section. Hypocrite men and women stirred up a lot of mischief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and His Messenger have the greatest right; once their intention in a matter is known, a person's own intention must yield to it.
rows.anchor: The right of God and His Messenger is the greatest. Hence, when in some matter, their intention is known

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger must urge people to follow God's directives and implement them, so he must obey a divine directive and disregard objections in the matter.
rows.anchor: The obligation of a messenger as God’s envoy is to urge people to God’s directives and to implement them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was told to put into practice the removal of the jāhiliyyah prohibition on marrying an adopted son's former wife and to disregard the resulting agitation.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) was directed to take practical steps to eradicate the concept regarding the wife of an adopted son

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muḥammad is the final prophet, all aspects of religion had to be completed through him without deficiency.
rows.anchor: Since Muḥammad (sws) was the last of God’s prophets, it was essential that all aspects of religion be brought to a completion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage delineates God's great favor in sending a Prophet and the obligations the community owes him.
rows.anchor: A delineation of God’s great favour to mankind by sending a Prophet to them and of the obligations this ummah owes to him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supplies a brief marriage history of Zaynab and Zayd first so later verse discussion need not pause for its details.
rows.anchor: a brief summary of the marriage of Zaynab (rta) and Zayd (rta) mentioned in these verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The translated couplet presents its speaker as willing to abandon worldly wealth and status to be accepted as the Prophet's slave.
rows.anchor: I swear by your friendship that if you accept me as your slave

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet freed Zayd, whom he had loved from the beginning for his qualities.
rows.anchor: After this, the Prophet (sws) set him free. He loved Zayd (rta) since the very beginning because of his qualities;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd sometimes governed Madīnah while the Prophet was absent.
rows.anchor: At times, he even remained the ruler of Madīnah in the absence of the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After freeing Zayd, the Prophet's affection grew further; observers consequently thought he had adopted Zayd as his son.
rows.anchor: when people saw his love and attention towards Zayd (rta), they thought that perhaps he has made Zayd (rta) his adopted son.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd had administrative and military ability: the Prophet appointed him to lead campaigns and sometimes govern Madīnah during his absence.
rows.anchor: At many instances, the Prophet (sws) deputed him as the leader of military campaigns.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet arranged Zayd's marriage to his cousin Zaynab as an act of favor and respect; her family objected to her marrying a freed slave of lower status, but the Prophet insisted to challenge such social assumptions, and she consented.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) wedded him to his paternal cousin, Zaynab bint Jaḥash (rta), to grant him favour and respect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites attacked the marriage of a noblewoman to a former slave, and especially tried to persuade Zaynab that the match was unjust; such malicious campaigning turned society against the reform.
rows.anchor: Hypocrite men and women launched this malicious propaganda that Muḥammad (sws) had wedded off a woman of noble descent to his liberated slave.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd's humility and self-esteem, combined with Zaynab's forceful temperament and the poisoned atmosphere, led him to believe she felt superior and disliked the marriage, so he considered divorce to relieve them both.
rows.anchor: Zayd (rta) began to think that Zaynab (rta) regards herself to be superior to him, and does not like this relationship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before acting on divorce, Zayd consulted the Prophet because he had arranged the marriage; Zayd said Zaynab showed pride in her family rank, which hurt him, but denied any other doubt.
rows.anchor: he thought of finding out the opinion of the Prophet (sws) too because it was he who had been instrumental in making this marriage happen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet firmly told Zayd not to divorce Zaynab and to fear God, since a personal impression alone was no valid reason for divorce.
rows.anchor: asked him to fear God in this matter because a mere personal impression is not a valid reason for divorce.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet wanted the marriage to succeed because he had initiated it for a noble purpose, in opposition to the hypocrites' hopes.
rows.anchor: he himself had initiated this marriage for the realization of a noble objective.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divorce would damage Zaynab's reputation and compound her grief after criticism for marrying a freed slave, since she would then be called that slave's divorcee.
rows.anchor: her grief would become twofold. First she had heard the reproaches of Hypocrite men and women

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeling responsible for the situation, the Prophet thought he should show Zaynab extra affection; if divorced, he considered marrying her to console her, but feared scandal over an adopted son's former wife and could not add another wife.
rows.anchor: the only option left to appease the emotions of Zaynab (rta) would be to marry her.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the Prophet's pleas, Zayd saw divorce as the only way to relieve Zaynab's distress and his own, and he divorced her.
rows.anchor: He thus divorced her. Zaynab (rta) was grief-stricken on this.

rows.speaker: Narratives
rows.claim: Narratives report that Zaynab spontaneously recited the words 'We are for God and to Him shall we return' when she heard of the divorce.
rows.anchor: Narratives say that when she heard of this divorce the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the divorce, the Prophet decided to marry Zaynab, but the jāhiliyyah rule against marrying an adopted son's wife and the possibility of public criticism complicated this decision; the excerpt ends mid-explanation.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws), as mentioned earlier, decided to marry Zaynab (rta) but because of the jāhiliyyah custom
